title: Robert Walpole (Paris) → Sir John Goodricke (Stockholm), 5-page letter on Franco-British relations and the Corsica affair, with part of the letter in cypher
correspondents: Robert Walpole (British diplomat in Paris) → Sir John Goodricke (British envoy at Stockholm)
shelfmark: Chicago History Museum Research Center, Small Manuscripts, CHS MSS Alpha Walpole, Robert B0020C (Gunther Estate Purchase 1923.1000); Primo record alma991000655679709882
folio_note: 1 item, 5 pp.; the catalogue says 'Cypher for portion of letter'; how much is cipher is not stated
status: CHM catalogue (Alma/Primo) notes 'Cypher for portion of letter'; no decipherment is mentioned. Not on DECODE (known.py: no hits for Walpole 1769/Goodricke 1769). Goodricke's own papers (Bodleian) are reported to hold cypher letters with transliteration, so a decipherment of this exact letter may exist in another set.
why: Cipher passage in a Paris-to-Stockholm letter of 1769 on Anglo-French relations, Corsica and the Canadian Catholics; a short, probably numerical British diplomatic cipher of the Northern Department, whose table could be rebuilt from the Goodricke/State Papers Foreign Sweden and France series.
score_note: Scored from the archive description during the Oct 2026 Chicago Pritzker/CHM/CPL sweep (research/chi_pritzker_chm_cpl/); not viewed
verify: Ask the CHM Research Center (research@chicagohistory.org) for a scan of CHS MSS Alpha Walpole B0020C; compare the cypher group shapes with the 1769 Walpole-Weymouth cipher letters in TNA SP 78 and the Goodricke papers at the Bodleian.
prior_art: open (checked 29 Oct 2026: web search Walpole/Goodricke 1769 cipher; CHM Primo; known.py; cryptiana not searched by name; the Bodleian Goodricke finding aid was reached only through a search snippet, its site refused automated access)
access_note: Small manuscript in the CHM Research Center (e-basement storage); no online images found; request a scan from research@chicagohistory.org

title: William Rattle Plum papers: 7 military telegraph cipher notebooks used by Capt. William G. Fuller and W. R. Plum, Department of the Tennessee, with 389 pp. of Fuller's letterpress copies
correspondents: William G. Fuller (Assistant Superintendent, Military Telegraph, Dept. of the Tennessee) and William R. Plum (telegraph operator, later author of The Military Telegraph during the Civil War, 1882)
place: Department of the Tennessee (Chattanooga / Nashville area)
shelfmark: Chicago History Museum Research Center, CHS MSS Lot William Rattle Plum B0602C #1/HB (acc. M1967.0702), 0.5 linear ft., 1 box; Primo record alma991000660089709882
folio_note: 7 notebooks (extent of each not stated); genre terms in the catalogue include 'Ciphers' and 'Notebooks'
status: Catalogue says 'military telegraph cipher notebooks used by Fuller and William Rattle Plum'; whether they hold enciphered telegrams or only the route-cipher tables is not stated. The Union Military Telegraph route/transposition ciphers are published (Plum 1882; Eckert and Stager books), so these are probably keys or working copies, not an open cipher. Not on DECODE; not in the repo (known.py hits for Plum are only the 1882 book).
why: Primary working notebooks of a Union Military Telegraph office in 1863-64 could add key variants and enciphered Chattanooga-campaign telegrams to the Union route-cipher corpus.
score_note: Scored from the archive description during the Oct 2026 Chicago Pritzker/CHM/CPL sweep (research/chi_pritzker_chm_cpl/); not viewed
verify: Ask the CHM Research Center what the notebooks contain (route-cipher tables vs enciphered telegrams) and whether they can be scanned; compare with Plum 1882 vol. 1 appendix and the Eckert books (targets/eckert1862).
prior_art: open (checked 29 Oct 2026: web search Plum/Fuller notebooks; Plum 1882 is the published description of the Union ciphers; contents of the notebooks not described anywhere found)
access_note: Archive box at the CHM Research Center; no online images found; request a scan or visit by appointment

title: Gen. Daniel Ruggles (CSA), orders to Maj. W.J. Anderson, Maj. St. Cuny, Maj. J.M. Quinlan, Capt. Quitman, Capt. Dashiell and Lt. H.H. Price to move troops, catalogued as 'possibly in code'
correspondents: Daniel Ruggles (Confederate brigadier general) → Maj. W.J. Anderson, Maj. St. Cuny, Maj. J.M. Quinlan, Capt. Quitman, Capt. Dashiell, Lt. H.H. Price
place: Columbus ([North Carolina?] in the CPL catalogue; Ruggles's 1864 command was in Mississippi/Alabama, so probably Columbus, Mississippi)
shelfmark: Chicago Public Library, Harold Washington Library Center, Special Collections, American Civil War Documents, Manuscripts, Letters and Diaries and Grand Army of the Republic Collection (spe-w00073), Series 1 Subseries CC, Box 8, Item 86.40.15
folio_note: 1 item; extent and how much is in code not stated ('orders to move troops, possibly in code')
status: CPL finding aid says 'possibly in code'; no decipherment mentioned. May turn out to be a clear text with abbreviations or a simple Confederate field cipher. Not on DECODE; known.py: no hits for Ruggles.
why: A Confederate field order of 1864 in what may be a short cipher; would be a rare Confederate (not Union) army-level cipher text outside the Richmond-level material.
